environment.description: Same application deployed on EC2 but origin is NOT publicly accessible. CloudFront distribution (d1234abcdef.cloudfront.net) is the sole entry point. Origin access is restricted via a custom header X-Origin-Verify with a rotating secret (AWS Secrets Manager, 24h rotation) that the ALB listener rule checks — requests without the matching header get 403. CloudFront behavior has a signed URL requirement: all requests to /api/directory/search must carry a valid CloudFront signed URL (RSA-SHA1, key pair ID K2ABCXYZ, policy restricts query string parameters to a whitelist of 'username' and 'department' with URL-encoded values matching ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]{1,64}$ enforced in the CloudFront Function at viewer-request stage). The CloudFront Function (cfn-input-gate-v3) performs regex validation on query parameters before forwarding; non-matching characters cause immediate 403. Origin request policy forwards only whitelisted query strings that passed the function gate.

config.hosting: EC2 t3.medium, Amazon Linux 2023, private subnet
config.origin_protection: X-Origin-Verify custom header, ALB listener rule rejects without match
config.signed_urls: Required for /api/* paths, RSA key pair K2ABCXYZ, 15min expiry
config.cloudfront_function: cfn-input-gate-v3: validates query params username/department against ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]{1,64}$, returns 403 on mismatch
config.origin_request_policy: forwards only username, department query strings that passed viewer-request function
config.secret_rotation: X-Origin-Verify rotates every 24h via Secrets Manager
config.network: ALB in private subnet, no public IP, SG allows only CloudFront managed prefix list
